decision_rule: this is a DESIGN assessment only; it does not select an implementation and does not authorize any production change; the shortest-schema option is NOT automatically preferred — direction C carries the highest requalification cost and unverified model compatibility

A_keep_original_v2.description: keep the full typed schema and frozen instructions unchanged
does_not_handle: to_status='completed' enum violation (reproduced as the sole attempt-2 blocker)
A_keep_original_v2.residual_risk: the input-level vocabulary collision (D* envelope 'status': 'completed') remains model-visible

B_vocabulary_guidance_candidate.description: instructions-only: state that to_status for questions must come from the frozen QuestionStatus vocabulary, that run/delegation 'completed' is a DIFFERENT state machine, map closure statuses to their policy requirements (answered->basis+disposition, unresolved->basis+limitations+summary, blocked->blocker) AND spell out the frozen QuestionDisposition vocabulary with the status/disposition mapping; schema unchanged
does_not_handle: attempt-1 abbreviated field NAMES (a vocabulary statement cannot force field-name choice)
evidence-less closures — irrelevant to B: the counterfactuals prove the policy layer rejects them regardless of what the model is told
B_vocabulary_guidance_candidate.grounding_policy_risk: none (policy unchanged; guidance only mirrors EXISTING frozen policy rules)
handles_observed_errors: attempt-2 to_status='completed' — the exact legal value list becomes instruction text BEFORE the first attempt

attempt-1's illegal disposition VALUE class (no_evidence_found) — the frozen QuestionDisposition members become prose (note: on THIS sample the disposition error co-occurred with naming errors, so class-level coverage only)
B_vocabulary_guidance_candidate.prompt_token_delta: small positive (a few hundred tokens of static rule text; measured before any authorization to implement
B_vocabulary_guidance_candidate.residual_risk: guidance increases instruction length; value lists in text can drift from the schema if enums ever change (mitigatable by deriving text from the enum at build time — implementation detail, not decided here)
B_vocabulary_guidance_candidate.runtime_identity_and_requalification_cos: production prompt change -> new INTEGRATE runtime identity -> requalification required (V3 discipline); zero schema migration

C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.description: RCA-2A.1 experimental contract (uniform update envelope, compact typed merged status enum, strict per-kind parse validation) while keeping per-kind member checks and server-side identity binding
does_not_handle: the VALUE vocabulary itself — 'completed' is illegal there too; if the model's priming persists it fails the same way (one retry instead of zero)
attempt-1 abbreviated field names (target_handle/to_status are still the required names)
disposition enum violations pass the retry boundary (untyped string; resolver fail-closed AFTER retry)
evidence-less closures (counterfactuals show the policy layer rejects them regardless of schema — unchanged by C)
C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.grounding_policy_risk: none observed on this sample (canonical actions identical post-resolver); the None-vs-[] basis distinction is preserved by the 2A.1 resolver
handles_observed_errors: attempt-2 to_status='completed' — merged enum rejects at parse with retry feedback (value list in the parse error)
union cascade noise — 6 variants instead of 10 branches; -38% model-face size (2A.1 measurement)
C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.output_tool_schema_change: YES — new model-facing schema (proposal envelope + merged enum)
C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.prompt_token_delta: negative on the model face (2A.1: approximately -38% schema tokens), instructions unchanged
C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.residual_risk: one sample cannot establish model compatibility with the envelope; a controlled comparison is the only honest way to measure
C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.resolver_rejection_change: new proposal-layer violation codes fire before the canonical resolver (P_STATUS_NOT_IN_KIND_ENUM observed on this sample)
C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.retry_feedback_change: parse-layer for merged status; RESOLVER-side (no retry) for disposition/foreign-field classes
C_strict_compact_typed_candidate.runtime_identity_and_requalification_cos: HIGHEST: new output contract -> new runtime identity -> full requalification; schema migration risk; equivalence proven offline (2A.1: 16/16) but model compatibility UNVERIFIED

hypothesis: priming/causality claims; model behavior under changed contracts
observed_real_model_behavior: the two raw payloads anchor every 'handles observed errors' row
unverified_model_reliability: ALL improvement/compatibility expectations — nothing here is a reliability measurement

final_disposition_rca2a5.basis: the confirmed failure layer is a status-vocabulary error (VOCABULARY_COLLISION_CONFIRMED as an input fact + MODEL_INVALID_STATUS_CHOICE_OBSERVED with the legal values schema-visible but never prose-visible, and the enum-value feedback cut off by the frozen retry budget); direction B targets exactly this class with zero schema change and the smallest requalification surface; direction C adds NO coverage for the observed value-vocabulary defect on this sample (identical accepted values) at the highest identity/requalification cost, and both proposal variants demonstrably DEMOTE disposition validation below the retry boundary
final_disposition_rca2a5.not_claimed: B's effectiveness is UNVERIFIED (one sample; needs a controlled real-model comparison under explicit new authorization); this is a design-evaluation conclusion, not a model qualification judgment and not an implementation approval
